text:
Sam (sales): FYI the ACME POC demo just failed during the upload step — client got a 413 and the UI shows truncated context. Trying to repro now.
Priya (solutions): Ugh. Is this the single multipart POST flow or presigned uploads?
Sam (sales): It's the presigned bundle flow we demoed yesterday. They sent a single huge JSON with base64 attachments in one request.
Marta (eng): 413 comes from our gateway/nginx layer usually. Can you paste the raw request size?
Sam (sales): Raw size ~24MB per bundle, they said. Server logs: 
```
[ERROR] 2026-03-21T14:12:02Z upstream returned 413: Request Entity Too Large
```
Priya (solutions): Ok — typical. Two options: client-side chunk + stitch on upload, or switch to true presign streaming with part uploads. The latter needs a tiny change in the demo code but keeps UI simple.
Alex (devex): Also check if the model context is what's getting clipped or if the payload is being rejected entirely. 24MB is big but still could be below some token limits once decoded. What encoding are they using?
Sam (sales): They used UTF-16LE for some reason (legacy exporter). That bloated it. After decoding it's ~40k tokens but with metadata it's hitting our max request size in the gateway.
Marta (eng): Two-pronged: 1) gateway/nginx has `client_max_body_size` default too small for 24MB in their env — we can raise on their dedicated demo route. 2) recommend they switch exporter to UTF-8 or compress payload (gzip) before presign upload.
Priya (solutions): For the customer-facing demo, I can ship a small patch to their client showing chunked presign flow. Alex — can you paste the minimal example we use in docs?
Alex (devex): Sure. Minimal pseudocode (send parts then POST manifest):
```
// get presigned URLs
let parts = await getPresignUrls(fileSize, chunkSize)
for (p of parts) await uploadPart(p.url, file.slice(p.start, p.end))
await postManifest({parts: parts.map(p => p.etag), meta})
```
Also add `Content-Encoding: gzip` on client if you can compress before uploading.
Sam (sales): Will send to ACME + ask them to try UTF-8 + gzip first. If they can't change client, we'll ask eng to bump `client_max_body_size` on the demo route.
Marta (eng): I can bump it temporarily on the demo host to 50M and watch metrics. If we see increased latency or errors we revert. Also adding nginx logs to trace exact bytes.
deploy-bot: deploy started: nginx-config/demo-route-update to staging -> success in 00:00:23
Marta (eng): Deployed change to demo staging. Sam, try the upload again and paste logs.
Sam (sales): Retried — now they get 200 on upload, but model output indicates the prompt is truncated mid-sentence. Body accepted but context still incomplete.
Alex (devex): That suggests tokenization/truncation at model service side. Check that the final assembled prompt size (tokens) is below our per-request token limit for the selected model. Which model are they using?
Sam (sales): Using `open-compat-3b` (demo). Estimated token count ~42k after utf16 decode and not compressed.
Marta (eng): `open-compat-3b` limit is 32k tokens in our serving profile. We'll need to either: a) cut before sending (smart truncation), b) enable streaming and maintain prefix caching, or c) split into multiple context-aware requests. For the demo, (a) + informative UI is fastest.
Priya (solutions): Can we auto-detect and present a warning in the demo: "Context exceeds model limit, trimming oldest messages"? That preserves UX.
Alex (devex): Yes — we have a small snippet we use in demos: compute token count (we use tiktoken-lite) and if > maxTokens, slice last N tokens and attach a system note "truncated earlier content".
Sam (sales): I'll push that change to the demo client and resend. Also asking ACME to switch exporter to UTF-8 + gzip.
Marta (eng): One more safeguard: if payload sizes are common for a customer, we can create a per-customer route with higher body limit and an alert for increased cost. I'll create a ticket to track: ENG-POC-413-ACME.
Priya (solutions): Thanks — will document the recommended presign chunk example in the POC runbook so AE's can ship it quickly.
Sam (sales): ACME confirms UTF-8 + gzip + client-side chunking works end-to-end. They see full context and no truncation. Demo passed. :tada:
Marta (eng): Nice. I'll close the temporary nginx change at EOD and leave the runbook note.
Sam (sales): Closing thread — thanks everyone for the quick swarm.
